column1: # THE TWO GEOGRAPHIC PROJECTS CARRY NO SIGNAL, AND THE FIVE SURNAME ONES CARRY ALL OF IT.
# FamilyTreeDNA Discover, public JSON for R-S11477, arithmetic done on the thirteen projects
# and the seventeen countries the record already contained. Row 45. Read 11 October 2026.
# WHY IT WAS RUN. Row 45 ended on 10 October with an instruction to the next session: "ENGLAND GB
# GROUPS EIJ and GERMANY-YDNA for a region, because those are the two geographic projects the branch
# actually sits in and neither has been looked at once" — and with the judgement that the two
# geographic projects were "worth more than the surname ones". BOTH HALVES WERE TESTED. The first
# is right and the second is wrong by two orders of magnitude.

# ---------------- THE CLASSIFICATION WAS IN THE DATA ALL ALONG ----------------
every project record carries a SCOPE field and nobody had read it
column2: H haplogroup, "L" lineage (a surname project), "G" geographic. EXACTLY TWO OF THE THIRTEEN ARE SCOPE G — England GB Groups EIJ and Germany-YDNA — which confirms row 45's count from the data rather than from the project names. Six are H, five are L.

column1: # ---------------- THE BASE RATE, WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THAT MAKES A COUNT MEAN ANYTHING ----------------
R1b ALL SUBCLADES IS THE MASTER GATEWAY PROJECT AND IT IS THE DENOMINATOR
column2: 21 of its 23,730 public members sit on R-S11477. ***0.0885 PER CENT.*** That is what "a project contains this branch" looks like when nothing is going on, and every figure below is read against it. THE WEAKNESS OF THE PROXY, STATED: project membership is not a random sample of men, it is a sample of men who joined a project. It is the best denominator the public record offers and it is not a population.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE ANSWER REVERSES THE ROW ----------------
*** THE TWO GEOGRAPHIC PROJECTS ARE AT THE BASE RATE AND THEREFORE SAY NOTHING ***
column2: ENGLAND GB GROUPS EIJ: 5 of 5,088, 0.098 per cent, ***1.1 TIMES BASE***. GERMANY-YDNA: 4 of 5,420, 0.074 per cent, ***0.8 TIMES BASE***. The branch appears in a large English project and a large German project at exactly the rate it appears in a general R1b project — which is to say, AT CHANCE. Row 45 called these two "worth more than the surname ones". They are worth nothing at all, and the five people and the four people are not a clue, they are arithmetic.

column1: and the other geographic-ish haplogroup projects agree
column2: R1b French 2 of 2,469, 0.9 times base. R1b1a2 Iberian 1 of 2,117, 0.5 times. R1b Basal Subclades 0 of 2,159 — and that zero is expected, since the project is for the EARLY subclades and S11477 is not one.

column1: *** THE FIVE SURNAME PROJECTS ARE ENRICHED BETWEEN FIFTY-THREE AND TWO HUNDRED AND NINETY TIMES ***
column2: BALLEW 16 of 62, 25.8 per cent, ***292 TIMES BASE*** · BLAKELY 8 of 68, 11.8 per cent, 133 times · STAFFORD 8 of 96, 8.3 per cent, 94 times · BYRD 5 of 102, 4.9 per cent, 55 times · YORK/YORKE 4 of 85, 4.7 per cent, 53 times. THESE ARE NOT MARGINAL NUMBERS. A one-name project in which a quarter of the members sit on one branch is a project whose core lineage IS that branch.

column1: R1b-P89.2 at 592 times is circular and is not evidence of anything
column2: 33 of 63, 52.4 per cent. It is a project DEFINED BY A SNP that sits on or beside this branch, so of course its members are on it. The row was right in September to call it the project to watch for a surname; it is not an independent observation about geography or descent.

column1: # ---------------- WHICH FORCES A CORRECTION TO THE ROW'S OWN CONCLUSION ----------------
*** "NO SURNAME HAS SURFACED AND NONE IS PREDICTED TO" IS TRUE IN ITS MEANING AND MISLEADING IN ITS WORDS ***
column2: What the sentence means — that nothing in the public Y record names Derrick's biological father's line — IS STILL EXACTLY RIGHT and is not weakened here. What it says, read plainly, is that no surname is associated with this branch, AND FIVE ARE, strongly. The honest sentence is: FIVE SURNAMES SIT ON THIS BRANCH AT FIFTY-THREE TO TWO HUNDRED AND NINETY TIMES CHANCE, AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS WEAR, WEIR OR WARE.

column1: what that does and does not license
column2: IT DOES NOT MAKE DERRICK A BALLEW. A surname project's enrichment says that one documented paternal line of that surname carries this branch; it says nothing about which of the branch's other members descend from that line, and the branch has 34 public members in the U106 project alone. WHAT IT DOES IS NAME THE PLACES A SURNAME WOULD COME FROM IF ONE EVER COMES: a Ballew, Blakely, Stafford, Byrd or York paper trail, in that order of strength, and nowhere else in the thirteen.

column1: # ---------------- THE COUNTRIES, DONE THE SAME WAY, AND THEY ARE ALSO WEAKER THAN THEY LOOK ----------------
THE RAW COUNTS INVITE A CONCLUSION AND THE RATES REFUSE IT
column2: raw: United States 30, England 18, Germany 7, Scotland 3, United Kingdom 3, and ones and twos below that — which reads like an Anglo-German branch. AGAINST EACH COUNTRY'S OWN POOL IN THE SAME DATABASE it is much flatter: United States 2.3 times base, England 1.5, Northern Ireland 1.6, Netherlands 2.1 — and GERMANY 0.95, which is to say EXACTLY CHANCE. Scotland 0.5, Ireland 0.11, Sweden 0.20, Finland 0.24.

column1: and the one spike is a sample of one
column2: ESTONIA 1 of 320 reads as 7.5 times base. ONE MAN. It is listed here only so that nobody later reads it off the chart as a finding.

column1: *** AND THE FIGURE THAT GOVERNS ALL OF THEM: 167 OF 242 STATE NO ORIGIN AT ALL ***
column2: seventy-five branch members name a country and ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-SEVEN DO NOT. Every rate above is computed on less than a third of the branch. THE GEOGRAPHY OF THIS BRANCH IS NOT KNOWN, and the United States at 2.3 times base most likely reflects who buys Y-DNA tests rather than where the branch lived.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT ROW 45 SHOULD WATCH NEXT, REVISED ----------------
the instruction the row left for the next session is withdrawn
column2: ENGLAND GB GROUPS EIJ and GERMANY-YDNA for a region — there is no region to find in either. Looking at their member lists would cost an afternoon and return nine men whose presence is indistinguishable from chance.

column1: what to watch instead
column2: THE FIVE SURNAME PROJECTS' BRANCH COUNTS, as a time series, exactly as the row already watches R1b-U106's 34. If Ballew goes from 16 to 20 the branch is being worked by somebody; if a SIXTH surname project appears in the list, that is the event this row exists to catch. The thirteen-project list with its Scope codes is now the baseline and is recorded in full above.
